items.title: Kenny Davern interviewed by Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, September 23, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Then it becomes a travesty, like the Elvis. Because that’s where they fail.

ctx.x: That’s macabre. Don’t laugh. It’s just as macabre in jazz life too, to see all these Charlie Parker clones come out. Did you ever hear of the guys who try to emulate Louis where they, Armstrong, where they really fail is when they try to do the vocalizations. Then it becomes a travesty, like the Elvis. Because that’s where they fail. Unless they just use their own natural voice. I mean if you want to quote that, like Ethel Waters did, “I Can’t Give You Anything But Love, Baby,” but she actually does scat Louis’…

Yes it makes a lot of sense. We are going to have to move here, because I know that we’ve got to wrap up this interview, but I’ve enjoyed talking to you. You’ve given us some marvelous insights. Say something to our young people about going into this music, if they find themselves as music majors in universities now. What are they going to have to face? And how to face it?
